$comment:
CARD CORPUS SCHEMA — draft 2020-12.

Authored against packages/engine/src/cards.ts (IdeologyCard, VoterCard,
ConspiracyCard, HeadlineCard) and packages/engine/src/state.ts (Delta,
Resource, Ideologue) as they stand today. It deliberately does NOT redesign the
engine types. Where a real card cannot be expressed by the Effect union, the card
was not fudged into the schema — it is recorded in packages/cards/KNOWN-GAPS.md.

DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE FROM cards.ts: every card carries two extra envelope fields,
`source` and `provenance`, which are NOT part of the engine card shapes. They exist
so a reviewer can tell recovered text from authored text, and packages/cards strips
them in toEngine*Card() before handing cards to the engine. See README.md.

Sources for every constraint are recorded inline as $comment, keyed to
docs/AUTHENTIC-SHASN-REFERENCE.md (REF) and docs/rules-reference.md (RULES).

Type test: test/engine-parity.test.ts asserts that the four resource keys in
$defs.delta are exactly Object.keys(IDEOLOGUE_RESOURCE) and that the effect op
enum in $defs.effect matches the Effect union in cards.ts. JSON Schema cannot import
a TypeScript type, so that drift guard lives in a test rather than in this file.
title: Shasn card corpus

deck.$comment: Deck id. Must equal the directory name under decks/; the loader asserts it.

campaign.$comment: campaign: string on IdeologyCard in cards.ts. Cards in one deck file share it.

card.$comment: A card is exactly one of the four engine card shapes plus the provenance envelope.

id.$comment:
Namespaced card id: <type>-<deck>-<index>.
  ig-*  IdeologyCard      vo-*  VoterCard
  ct-*  ConspiracyCard    hl-*  HeadlineCard

Modelled on the printed card-code convention recovered at REF 5.7
(IG10.108 = India, print generation 10, card 108; AM10.100 = America).
The engine treats CardID as an opaque string (state.ts), so the shape is free to
choose, but keeping it stable across editions makes a corpus diff readable.
scripts/validate.ts additionally checks the type prefix and the deck segment, so a
misfiled card is a build failure rather than a confusing lookup miss.

source.$comment:
Where this card's material came from. Mandatory on every card.
For verbatim/adapted cards this is the document id or URL in
docs/AUTHENTIC-SHASN-REFERENCE.md 4 plus the section that yielded it.
For inferred cards it is the register source: 'original; register per REF 8.2'.

Enforced as an error because REF 9.2 is explicit that shipping unattributed
recovered text is the single highest legal risk in this repository.

provenance.$comment:
verbatim  — card name and rules text reproduced word-for-word from a cited
            official 'X Cards Explained' document. REF 4.1/4.2.1/4.3.
adapted   — recovered text, but the card as played here is a reconstruction: an
            option was dropped, a branch was flattened, or only one side of an
            Ideology Card was recovered and the other is authored. REF 2.4 records
            that ZERO ordinary question Ideology Cards were recovered in full, so
            every Ideology Card in this corpus is at best `adapted`.
inferred  — authored here. The register is copied from REF 8.2; the content is not
            Memesys'.

campaign_ref.$comment: campaign: string on IdeologyCard in cards.ts. Cross-checked against the deck file's own `campaign` by scripts/validate.ts.

advisory.$comment: cards.ts Advisory. REF 2.2 confirms a Content Advisory flag exists on Ideology Cards and that the table may vote flagged cards out before play (RULES p14). REF 10 item 4 records that the LEGEND for the two tiers was never recovered — these two tier names are the engine's own invention, not recovered values.

resource.$comment: Resource in state.ts. RULES p11/p33: the four resources map one-to-one onto the four Ideologues (Capitalist->Funds, Supremo->Clout, Showstopper->Media, Idealist->Trust). See $defs.ideologueResourceMap; test/engine-parity.test.ts fails if this enum and IDEOLOGUE_RESOURCE ever disagree.

ideologue.$comment: Ideologue in state.ts. RULES p13: 'Every answer will yield a different set of resources', and both answers on a card belong to different Ideologues.

ideologueResourceMap.$comment:
The one-to-one Ideologue -> Resource map, stated as data so that it is auditable and
so that the four branches of $defs.ideologySide can be read against it.
Source: RULES p11 & p33; mirrored in state.ts as IDEOLOGUE_RESOURCE.

This is the mapping the schema cross-checks `ideologue` against — see
$defs/ideologySide. A test asserts this object's values equal Object.keys/values of
IDEOLOGUE_RESOURCE, so a change to the engine's map is a test failure, not a
silently-wrong card corpus.

delta.$comment:
Delta = Partial<Record<Resource, number>> (state.ts). Sparse on purpose.

maximum 9: REF 5.2 observes real payouts of 2-5 discs in total and 0-3 of any
single type, printed as one disc per unit and never as a numeral. 9 is a generous
ceiling, not an observed value.

minimum 0: a negative payout is not expressible in the engine. Losing resources is a
`lose` effect on a Conspiracy/Headline card, not a payout (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md 6.2).

NO minProperties here. `{}` is a schema-valid but design-invalid side; that is
deliberately the balance checker's job (D5 EMPTY_SIDE), not the schema's, so that
shape validation and design judgement stay separately reviewable.
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md 6.2 argues for exactly this split.

nonEmptyDelta.$comment: A Delta with at least one resource in it. Used for an Effect's `res` payload, where an empty delta would be a silent no-op — unlike an Ideology Card's `pays`, where `{}` is a legitimate (if bad) design statement the balance checker owns.

answer.$comment:
The real answer register, enforced rather than merely described.
REF 8.2 rule 1: 'Answers open with the bare word "Yes." or "No."' — REF
inspected 20+ recovered answers and not one opens any other way.
REF 8.2 rule 2 requires deadpan, not jokey, and rule 3 caps the answer at 15
words after the Yes/No, hence maxLength 200 rather than a word-count rule.

This is a real fidelity constraint, not a style preference: an answer that does
not open with Yes/No is a card we did not recover correctly.

oneOf.$comment: Capitalist -> Funds (RULES p11/p33). The side must STATE its own resource explicitly, even when zero.

ideologySide.$comment:
THE IDEOLOGUE / RESOURCE CROSS-CHECK. Each branch of `oneOf` pins `ideologue` to a
constant and REQUIRES the resource that Ideologue maps to (see
$defs.ideologueResourceMap) to be named in `pays`.

Requiring the key to be PRESENT does not mean requiring it to be POSITIVE, and that
distinction is load-bearing. REF 5.2 verifies from the official 432-card marketing
render that the shipped card 'SHOULD WE INVADE NEW SPAIN?' has a CAPITALIST side
paying 2 Trust + 1 Media and ZERO Funds. A rule of the form 'a Capitalist answer must
pay at least 1 Funds' would reject a real, shipped card. So the schema demands the
author state the zero rather than demanding it not be zero.

REF 5.2 also notes that `{trust: 0}` and `{}` are otherwise indistinguishable in the
data, and that the real game avoids the ambiguity by always printing at least one
disc. Requiring the key makes the zero explicit at authoring time; the 'at least one
disc' half of that rule is enforced as D5 EMPTY_SIDE by scripts/balance.ts.

question.$comment: REF 8.2 rule 3: the real question is a yes/no policy dilemma of at most ~12 words, never a question about tactics. maxLength 200 leaves room for the longest observed ('SHOULD WOMEN BE FREE TO HAVE CHILDREN SINGLE OR IN A RELATIONSHIP?'). REF 5.1 confirms the engine's {question, sides} model is already an exact match for the printed card.

sides.$comment: readonly [IdeologySide, IdeologySide] in cards.ts. A fixed-length array, never a keyed object — docs/ARCHITECTURE.md 6.2 explains why a keyed object would let card.sides[action.side] return undefined at runtime, in a live game, on a card nobody tested.

allOf.$comment:
RULES p13: the two answers on a card belong to two DIFFERENT Ideologues.
Four `contains` clauses with maxContains 1 = at most one side per Ideologue, and
with exactly two sides over four Ideologues that is precisely 'two different'.

REF 2.3 [INFERRED] from 14 tournament hands that Idealist and Supremo occupy
largely DISJOINT question space (6 of 14 hands are Idealist>0, Supremo=0), i.e.
the real corpus is a curated pairing table rather than 6 random pairs of 4. That
is a corpus-frequency property, not a per-card validity rule, so it is NOT
enforced here; scripts/balance.ts reports the realised pair distribution instead.

cost.$comment:
cost: Delta, structurally CONFIRMED CORRECT by REF 5.5: 'VoterCard = { cost:
Delta, voters: number } is structurally correct [VERIFIED votercards.png]'. The
printed front is a black field with a column of resource discs and one large
cream numeral.

minProperties 1, unlike IdeologyCard `pays`: a Voter Card that costs nothing is
not a card the physical product has, and an empty cost is almost always a typo'd
or omitted key rather than a design statement.

Every key is minimum 1, so a cost of {funds: 0} is rejected here rather than
silently paying nothing.

REF 3 and REF 10 item 3: the real 60-card cost distribution was never recovered,
so no total-cost constraint is asserted. scripts/balance.ts reports the realised
cost-per-voter curve so the shape is visible.

voters.$comment: RULES p10: 'Voter Cards can contain 1, 2 or 3 voters.' REF 3 confirms the 1/2/3 split is load-bearing: several real effects discriminate BY SIZE (Lab-Grown Earworm, Power Trip, Don't Kiss The Babies, Eradicating Germs, Fatality), so this is an enum and not a range.

effectTarget.$comment: EffectTarget in cards.ts. 'leader' = the player holding the most majority voters; ties give nobody. REF 4.4 item 2 records that this four-value enum does not fit several real cards (ON THE "HIGH" SEAS attaches to the card, A CALL FROM KARACHI auctions, NEXT BILLION DATA POINTS votes) — see packages/cards/KNOWN-GAPS.md.

effectDuration.$comment: EXECUTED. EffectDuration in cards.ts. reduce.ts installLiveEffects turns a lasting duration into a GameState.liveEffects entry whose activeFrom / expiresAt are absolute turn numbers computed at install, and advanceTurn drops it when the turn passes expiresAt. 'this-turn' is the default and is what the engine always did: resolve the effects once, discard the card. EXECUTABLE_DURATIONS in packages/cards/src/executable.ts is the registry, and it currently accepts all four. See KNOWN-GAPS.md G9 and G22.

effectTiming.$comment: EXECUTED, for two of the three values. EffectTiming in cards.ts. 'now' (the default) installs the effect live immediately; 'next-turn' keeps it dormant until the owner's next turn, using state.ts ownerNextTurn. 'after-this-turn' has no anchor — it would need a queue of effects to run between advanceTurn and the next player's first action, and nothing in the corpus needs one, so EXECUTABLE_TIMINGS refuses it. See KNOWN-GAPS.md G22.

effectTrigger.$comment: EXECUTED. EffectTrigger in cards.ts, carried on every Effect as `when`. installLiveEffects writes the effect into GameState.liveEffects and fireTriggers — a bounded cascade, one effect per wave, capped by TRIGGER_MAX_WAVES — applies it when the event is raised. EXECUTABLE_TRIGGERS in packages/cards/src/executable.ts is the registry of the events the reducer actually raises, because a `when` that is never raised installs a hook that never wakes. See KNOWN-GAPS.md G14.

effectCondition.$comment:
Narrowing on the event that woke a hook, ANDed across the keys present. EffectCondition in cards.ts.

byOwner: the event's actor is the effect's own owner. POWER TRIP is 'every time YOU influence a 3-Voter Card', which is byOwner plus influencedVotersAtLeast: 3 — the two keys are separate because the real card needs both at once.

influencedVotersAtLeast: the Voter Card that was bought carried at least this many voters. Only meaningful on 'on-voter-influenced'.

movedMyVoter: the voter the event moved belongs to the owner. GROWING DISSENT is 'every time any opponent Gerrymanders your voters'. Only meaningful on 'on-gerrymander'.

minProperties 1: an empty condition constrains nothing, and a card that writes one reads as though it narrowed something.

computedCount.$comment:
EXECUTED. A count read out of player state instead of written on the card. ComputedCount in cards.ts, read by resolveCount / computedValue in reduce.ts, always against the player the effect resolves FOR.

your-pool: the total resources that player holds.

ideologue-level: 1, 3 or 5, from the number of Ideology CARDS that player has answered. THIS IS NOT THE BALANCE CHECKER'S RESOURCE PROXY. The engine's real unlock rule is powers.ts hasPower, which counts CARDS answered and not resources paid, so a player who answers three Capitalist cards unlocks Prospecting whatever those cards paid and a player who answers one Capitalist card paying 3 Funds unlocks nothing. KNOWN-GAPS.md §6 sets out why D3's resource proxy over-reports, and reading resources here would make a card agree with the checker and disagree with the engine.

your-gerrymander-rights: moves still available across every zone the player leads, summed. p16 gives rights to a strict leader and nobody to a tie, so a zone they do not lead contributes zero.

volatile-voters: their pegs in Volatile Areas. p18 makes those permanent, so it only grows.

held-of-each-resource: for `per` only — what the player holds OF THE RESOURCE BEING GAINED. A `res` of 1 in each resource with this multiplier is IF YOU LIKE PIÑA COLADA's doubling of the whole mat, and the cap still applies on top, which is the card's own second sentence. EXECUTABLE_COMPUTED_SOURCES in packages/cards/src/executable.ts is the registry, and it also refuses `per` on any source but this one, because `per` multiplies each component of `res` and any other source would multiply a single number into four resources. See KNOWN-GAPS.md G15 and G4.

interrupt.$comment:
PARTIALLY EXECUTED. Interrupt in cards.ts, deliberately NOT in Effect[]: REF 5.4 and the recovered card text agree that a BLOCK, a DEFLECT, an AUCTION, a VOTE and a PASS change WHICH PHASE OF PLAY IS RUNNING, not how many resources anyone holds, so no parameterisation of the effect list expresses them. What changed is that there is now a phase for two of them to happen in.

EXECUTED: `block` and `deflect`. reduce() runs a response window — a played card whose effect list somebody could answer is HELD in GameState.interrupt, and RESPOND_INTERRUPT plays a held BLOCK or DEFLECT into it (a BLOCK cancels the staged resolution outright, including a lasting clause; a DEFLECT resolves the effect list for a named third player instead). PASS_INTERRUPT declines, and the window closes on the first answer or when every player it is waiting on has declined. The card is still a Conspiracy Card and still played face up out of turn, so this is the p19 window the rules already describe.

REFUSED, each for a reason the validator names: `auction` (needs a PlayerState debt field, an IOU, and a ruling on p12 read against a bid the bidder cannot afford — a rules system, not an op), `vote` (needs a ballot, a no-self-vote rule, a re-vote-on-tie loop, and a payoff that is G20 card movement — so it buys no card alone), `pass-card` (has no referent: it needs G12's in-flight queue and G20's move-card).

THE ENUMS WERE NARROWED, and that is the honesty gate rather than tidying. `window` lost 'out-of-turn' because RESPOND_INTERRUPT already refuses the actor of a card, which was the whole of its meaning; `target` lost 'any-player' because it is indistinguishable from 'any-card' in every position the window can be in. A value reduce() cannot act on is a declaration the engine ignores, which is the exact failure this schema's registry exists to prevent. EXECUTED_INTERRUPT_OPS / _WINDOWS / _TARGETS in packages/cards/src/executable.ts are the registries, and test/reducer-parity.test.ts re-derives all three from reduce.ts's own source text. See KNOWN-GAPS.md G13.

count.$comment: The `n` of a non-resource Effect. minimum 1: every op in the union is a gain or a loss of N, and a zero-N effect is a no-op that deserves to fail review. maximum 9 matches the delta ceiling; no recovered real card exceeds 4.

countOrComputed.$comment: A literal count, or the computed form (see $defs.computedCount). BOTH are executable: reduce() resolves the computed form against the player the effect resolves for, before it constructs a Choice.count or a loop bound, so the engine only ever sees a number. This is Count in cards.ts, and the widening of `n` from `number` is safe precisely because of that resolution step — KNOWN-GAPS.md G15 originally proposed NOT widening it, on the grounds that TypeScript would then stop a computed count reaching the engine. The resolution step is what keeps that guarantee, and $defs/computedCount is where the sources are documented.

effect.$comment:
The Effect union in packages/engine/src/cards.ts.

NOTE FOR REVIEWERS: the task brief calls this a '12-op union'. cards.ts as of this
commit declares 13 (gain, lose, gain-any, lose-any, steal-any, voters, evict,
discard-voter, convert-voter, gerrymander, draw-conspiracy, refresh-market,
discount). The schema follows cards.ts, because the engine is the contract. See
src/effect-ops.ts for the compile-time drift guard.

What this union CANNOT express is the subject of packages/cards/KNOWN-GAPS.md:
tokens-on-a-card, hostages, timed pass, auction, vote, out-of-turn reactive
block/deflect, dynamic COST modifiers, set collection, borrowed powers, delayed
cross-turn payoffs, and any effect aimed at something other than
you/each-opponent/everyone/leader. REF 5.4 puts that at roughly 40% of real
Conspiracy/Headline effects.

CLOSED SINCE THIS COMMENT WAS WRITTEN, kept so the next reader does not re-derive
it: duration and timing (G9/G22), when / until / condition (G14), target on
gerrymander (G8) and a computed n or per (G15/G4) are all EXECUTED.

THE THREE STATES, and which one every part of this schema is in:
  (a) expressible AND executed by reduce(): every op below, carrying only the fields
      EXECUTED_OPS in packages/cards/src/executable.ts says the case actually reads,
      plus the scope fields SCOPE_FIELDS_READ_BY_INSTALL says installLiveEffects
      reads, plus a computed n/per naming a source EXECUTABLE_COMPUTED_SOURCES
      implements.
  (b) expressible and validated but NOT executed: `interrupt`, and `timing:
      'after-this-turn'`. The schema ACCEPTS these so an author gets the engine
      explanation instead of 'unknown property'; packages/cards/src/validate.ts then
      REJECTS them, with the reason. No shipped card may use one.
  (c) not expressible at all: auction, vote, hostage, token piles, deck search, zone
      scoping, set collection. See KNOWN-GAPS.md G3/G6/G10/G11/G12/G16/G17/G18/G20.
packages/cards/test/reducer-parity.test.ts reads reduce.ts and re-asserts (a) over the
whole shipped corpus, so this list cannot drift away from the reducer.

oneOf.$comment: steal-any's `target` is the SET OF VICTIMS: with no target the thief picks the victim (Choice.from = null), with a target one theft decision is raised per resolved player and Choice.from is fixed, which is what makes 'take N from EVERY opponent' writable. It cannot mean 'donate to a chosen player' — that is G1.

G8, closed on BOTH the type and the reducer. gerrymander was the only resource-shaped op in cards.ts with no `target`, which is why "starting with you, every player can Gerrymander 1" (SUBMERGED / NEW FACE WHO DIS, REF 4.3) could not be written at all. applyEffect now loops resolveTargets(), so any EffectTarget is honoured. NOTE the grant lands in PlayerState.powerUses, which advanceTurn resets at the start of each player's own turn — so a cross-player grant is only spendable by the player whose turn the card resolved on. See KNOWN-GAPS.md G8 and G9.

draw-conspiracy's `from: 'discard'` is G17: the discard-pile reach that SELECTIVE ACCESS MEMORY needs. The top of a discard pile is the most recently discarded card, because that is the order discardTo pushes them in; choosing ANY card from the pile would need a decision over the pile's contents, which is a Choice kind this engine does not have. `target` says who receives the card.

`onlyIfEmpty` is G17's other half and is what makes AS CLEAR AS WATER (REF 4.3) expressible: a resolved player already holding a Conspiracy Card is skipped. It reads the RECIPIENT's hand, which is hidden from every viewer including its owner (playerView blanks it), so it is a fact no client can see and reduce() logs nothing on this path. It can only move a card out of the draw pile into an EMPTY hand, so it is bounded by the draw pile's own length.
refresh-market is the only op with no payload.

G5. `restrict` is the one op that is not a change to a pool, a mat or the board: it writes a `PlayerState.restrictions` entry, and INFLUENCE and BUY_CONSPIRACY are the two actions that consult it. `no-purchases` refuses both outright; `surcharge` adds `value` to the computed cost, ON TOP of any Helping Hands discount — Helping Hands is the Idealist's own L3 power (p32, 'reduce the cost of any purchase'), so letting it discount somebody else's tax would let a player buy their way out of another player's card.

'no-power' is a THIRD consult point and not this paragraph's subject: it is read by usesLeft() in packages/engine/src/powers.ts, which every POWER_* case in reduce() already asks, so the restriction is TOTAL over the whole power vocabulary and returns zero for every power the player holds. That totality is the dropped clause of GENDER TROUBLE - naming ONE Level 3 power is a decision over powers, which is G1. See RestrictionKind in packages/engine/src/state.ts.

`owed` is the KHAKI TERROR condition and is the field the soft-lock ruling lives in: it is what the card ASKS for, and the engine decrements the remaining amount by what was ACTUALLY donated, because `lose` never takes more than the player holds. Decrementing by the ask would make the only card that can clear the lock unplayable for anyone short of 4 of every type. See `Restriction` in packages/engine/src/state.ts, which carries the full argument.

`until` is the lifetime and is read HERE rather than by installLiveEffects: a restriction is not a live effect — it has no trigger and no effect list, and a hook that fired on an event could not refund a price. Expiry is ticked in advanceTurn alongside live effects, using the same absolute-turn arithmetic, so all four durations work with no special case and a replay reproduces it.

G20. `move-card` is the only op that changes WHICH Ideology Card exists rather than what a player may do with one, so both its enums are rulings and not formatting.

`from` has exactly one value, 'draw', and the reason it is not 'discard' is the whole security content of the op. The top of the Ideology DISCARD pile is the most recently ANSWERED card — ANSWER is the only thing that puts one there — and p13 makes an answered card face up under its owner's mat. Moving a discard-pile card into a player's hand would not restore the blind answer, it would publish it: the whole table would already know the question and the answer the holder is about to commit to. A card in the DRAW pile has never been answered, so nothing about it is public.

That choice also closes a leak for free. A hand is drained at the turn boundary INSTEAD OF a draw, so a card entering a hand must have left the draw pile already, for the deck to fall by exactly one per turn. Off the discard it would fall by one on the turn a card moved in and by none on the turn it was dealt — a discontinuity an observer could time, disclosing that a transfer had happened. Off the draw the count is monotonic and there is nothing to read.

`to` has two values and no third. A moved Ideology Card is HELD AND HIDDEN from every viewer INCLUDING its holder (see PRIVATE_PLAYER_KEYS and the ruling on PlayerState.ideologyCards in packages/engine/src/state.ts), or it leaves the game. A 'manifesto' or 'pending' destination would put a public card in the hidden zone, and neither is expressible. 'destroy' emits no LogEntry and no GameEvent, because a line announcing that a card with two unrevealed answers left the world is itself a disclosure.

The same source is HONEST for Conspiracy Cards and a LEAK for Ideology Cards: a Conspiracy Card is bought and held, never answered face up, so `draw-conspiracy`'s `from: 'discard'` discloses nothing. The difference is entirely p13.

name.$comment: REF 4.4 item 5: real cards name themselves in ALL CAPS, set as a title separate from the body. REF 8.1: the name is a pun, a reference or a throwaway joke, never a label. Case is not asserted because the reference doc transcribes names in title case; the renderer upper-cases.

text.$comment: cards.ts: 'Player-facing rules text. Must describe exactly what `effects` does.' The 20-word floor is a proxy for that — an effect list with no prose beside it is a card nobody can play. Where an adapted card drops part of the real effect, `text` describes what the effect list actually does and `source` names what was dropped.

cost.$comment: RULES p19: 'Cost any 4-5 resources, the number printed on the back of the card.' REF 5.5 confirms the cost is printed on the card back (photo shows a magenta back with 5 in the corner). Bounded rather than enum 4|5 so a future edition with a 6 does not need a schema edit.

excludeInTwoPlayer.$comment: cards.ts: 'p27: cards marked 2x are removed in the two-player game.'

headlineCard.$comment:
HeadlineCard = ConspiracyCard minus `cost`. REF 5.5 confirms that is correct:
'Headline Cards have no cost'.

RULES p18: a Headline is resolved at the end of the turn of the player who placed a
voter into a Volatile Area, one per voter, in the order the voters were placed.

REF 4.3 preamble, verified: Headlines are always carried out chronologically and in
the post-turn phase unless the card says otherwise; if a headline involves several
turns or several players a Block must be applied at the very beginning; donated
voters must be placed immediately. None of that is representable here — see
packages/cards/KNOWN-GAPS.md. `duration` and `timing` are now EXECUTED: a lasting
`duration` installs a GameState.liveEffects entry that advanceTurn expires, and
`timing` decides when it may first act. `interrupt` is still inert in reduce(), and
it exists so that an author who reaches for one gets the engine explanation from
the validator rather than 'unknown property'.
